result.topic_en: Euler treats the third order of his double series (m+n=4), with the cases m=3, n=1 and m=n=2. He combines his two methods to express the double sums ∫(1/z^2)(1/y^2) and ∫(1/z^3)(1/y) in terms of products of simple sums and ∫1/z^4, obtaining two different expressions for ∫(1/z^3)(1/y).
result.transcription:
SERIES SINGVLARES. 153
Ordo tertius, quo $m+n=4$.
13. Duo casus hic sunt considerandi, quorum primus est $m=3$, et $n=1$, vnde forma $\int\frac{1}{z^3}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z}$
$-\int\frac{1}{z^4}$ in hanc resoluitur:
$+\int\frac{1}{z^3}\left(\frac{1}{y}\right)-2\int\frac{1}{z^2}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^2}+\int\frac{1}{z}\left(\frac{1}{y^3}\right)+1\int\frac{1}{z^2}\left(\frac{1}{y^2}\right)+\int\frac{1}{z^3}\left(\frac{1}{y}\right)$
ita vt sit
$2\int\frac{1}{z^3}\left(\frac{1}{y}\right)+\int\frac{1}{z^2}\left(\frac{1}{y^2}\right)+\int\frac{1}{z}\left(\frac{1}{y^3}\right)=2\int\frac{1}{z^2}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^2}+\int\frac{1}{z^3}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z}-\int\frac{1}{z^4}$.
Ex prima autem methodo habetur
$\int\frac{1}{z^3}\left(\frac{1}{y}\right)+\int\frac{1}{z}\left(\frac{1}{y^3}\right)=\int\frac{1}{z^3}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z}+\int\frac{1}{z^4}$
quae aequalitas ab illa ablata relinquit
$\int\frac{1}{z^3}\left(\frac{1}{y}\right)+\int\frac{1}{z^2}\left(\frac{1}{y^2}\right)=2\int\frac{1}{z^2}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^2}-2\int\frac{1}{z^4}$.
Altero casu est $m=2$ et $n=2$, vnde colligitur
$\int\frac{1}{z^2}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^2}-\int\frac{1}{z^4}$
$=2\int\frac{1}{z^2}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^2}-\int\frac{1}{z^2}\left(\frac{1}{y^2}\right)-2\int\frac{1}{z^3}\left(\frac{1}{y}\right)$
$+2\int\frac{1}{z^2}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^2}-\int\frac{1}{z^2}\left(\frac{1}{y^2}\right)-2\int\frac{1}{z^3}\left(\frac{1}{y}\right)$
hincque porro
$2\int\frac{1}{z^2}\left(\frac{1}{y^2}\right)+4\int\frac{1}{z^3}\left(\frac{1}{y}\right)=3\int\frac{1}{z^2}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^2}+\int\frac{1}{z^4}$.
At methodus prima dat
$2\int\frac{1}{z^2}\left(\frac{1}{y^2}\right)=\int\frac{1}{z^2}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^2}+\int\frac{1}{z^4}$
vnde concludimus fore
$\int\frac{1}{z^2}\left(\frac{1}{y^2}\right)=\frac{1}{2}\int\frac{1}{z^2}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^2}+\frac{1}{2}\int\frac{1}{z^4}$
et $\int\frac{1}{z^3}\left(\frac{1}{y}\right)=\frac{1}{2}\int\frac{1}{z^2}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^2}$.
Superior vero conclusio suppeditat
$\int\frac{1}{z^3}\left(\frac{1}{y}\right)=\frac{3}{2}\int\frac{1}{z^2}\cdot\int\frac{1}{z^2}-\frac{5}{2}\int\frac{1}{z^4}$
Tom. XX. Nou. Comm. V quae

items.quote:

items.english: Subtracting this equation from the former leaves ∫(1/z^3)(1/y) + ∫(1/z^2)(1/y^2) = 2∫1/z^2·∫1/z^2 − 2∫1/z^4.
